original_question: For a body moving freely in Newtonian aerodynamics in R^n through a rarefied medium, what are the correct dynamical equation or equations governing the coupled evolution of the body and the surrounding particle distribution, and can one prove existence and uniqueness for those equations?
target_in_paper: Alexander Plakhov’s open problem titled "equations of motion in a rarefied medium": determine the dynamical equation(s) for a body moving freely in the framework of Newtonian aerodynamics in R^n, n >= 1, through a rarefied medium, and prove an existence-and-uniqueness theorem; the paper also isolates the 1-dimensional case in terms of the state (mu_t, X(t), P(t)).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the Newtonian-aerodynamics setting, the free motion of the body in R^n through a rarefied medium, the need for coupled body/medium dynamics, and the central mathematical goal of formulating the governing equation(s) and proving existence and uniqueness.
missing_details: The paper states the dimension range explicitly: n >= 1.
The official paper formulation is an open problem asking one to determine the equation(s) of dynamics and prove existence/uniqueness; it is not presented as an already established model.
The immediately preceding Plakhov problem supplies the intended Newtonian-aerodynamics context: a solid body interacting with a rarefied medium of point particles by elastic reflection.
To make the question stand-alone, one should say that the particle distribution is a phase-space distribution, not just a spatial distribution.
In the paper’s particular 1-dimensional case, the state is exactly the triple (mu_t, X(t), P(t)).
There mu_t is a measure on R^2 with coordinates (x,v), describing the distribution of infinitesimal particles at time t.
In that 1-dimensional particular case, the massive particle has mass 1.
The paper identifies P(t)=X'(t) as the velocity of the massive particle, so both position and velocity are part of the state.
The nearby context also clarifies the collision law: impacts are elastic, understood via the usual billiard reflection law in an inertial frame where the impact point is instantaneously at rest.

If one wants the body model made explicit, the neighboring Newtonian-aerodynamics problem treats the body as a solid body; in the explicit planar setup it is a compact domain with piecewise smooth boundary and uniformly distributed mass.
refined_question: In the framework of Newtonian aerodynamics, formulate the coupled evolution equations for a body moving freely in R^n, with n >= 1, through a rarefied medium of infinitesimal particles interacting with the body by elastic reflection, and prove an existence-and-uniqueness theorem for this dynamics. In particular, for n = 1, formulate the evolution of the state (mu_t, X(t), P(t)), where mu_t is a measure on R^2_(x,v) describing the particle distribution at time t, X(t) is the position of a massive point of mass 1, and P(t)=X'(t) is its velocity, and prove existence and uniqueness for that evolution.
justification: The draft is targeting Plakhov’s problem "equations of motion in a rarefied medium" almost verbatim. What it omits are the paper’s explicit dimension condition n >= 1, the exact 1D state variables, and the fact that the intended interaction model is inherited from the immediately preceding Newtonian-aerodynamics problem: a body/particle system with elastic reflections. Adding those details makes the question mathematically stand-alone while keeping it as narrow as the paper itself.
